newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Grenade attack wounds two in Sri Lanka refugee camp.
newsitem.headline: Grenade attack wounds two in Sri Lanka refugee camp.

text.p: Two Sri Lankan home guards were wounded on Monday in a suspected Tamil Tiger guerrilla grenade attack at a refugee camp in the northcentral town of Vavuniya, police and residents said.

"Someone threw a grenade at the police guard post at the entrance to the refugee camp near the railway station in the heart of the town," a resident said. "Fortunately there were no civilians there at the time. Otherwise many more would have been hurt."
The frontline town, gateway to the mainly rebel-held northern mainland, was tense after the attack around 3.00 p.m. (0900 GMT), he said.
Police said they believed the attack was carried out by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebel infiltrators.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
A Defence Ministry statement said on Monday that at least one rebel was killed when navy patrol blew up a guerrilla boat in the waters off eastern Mullaitivu on Saturday.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the number is higher.
